newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA says no govt guarantee on bank deposits.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA says no govt guarantee on bank deposits.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia deputy governor Graeme Thompson said on Thursday that something should be done to reduce a perception among the Australian public that there was a government guarantee on their bank deposits.

"I certainly think it would be worth doing something to reduce the community perception that there is a guarantee," Thompson said, when asked if banks enjoyed an advantage over other financial institutions.
Asked if there was a perception that bank depositors had a "quasi-guarantee", Thompson said that the central bank's role in this regard should made clearer.
"The community expects a level of prudential supervision of deposit taking institutions," Thompson said.

"When things go wrong in that area there's an expectation that government and official agencies ... will be in there, if not guaranteeing against failure (of the institution), at least reducing the likelihood," he said.
Australian banks are required to keep a minimum eight percent of their risk weighted assets as capital.
